_draft_note: DRAFT — coach to author. A starter cue library so the lesson-capture tool has something to pick from and so the wording rule is demonstrated. RULE, from the motor-learning literature and binding on every cue the app ever utters: EXTERNAL FOCUS ONLY — the ball, the target, the wall, the rhythm, an object. Never a body part, never a joint angle. 'Send the ball past the line' teaches; 'extend your elbow' does not. Each cue names the deviations it is commonly used against; which cue works for which player is exactly the thing the lesson data exists to find out. See docs/TEACHING-PLAN.md, Step 3, decision 9.

cues.text: Be turned before the ball bounces.
Racket back by the bounce, then wait.
Meet the ball out in front of you, where you can see it.
Let the ball come to your side, not your stomach.
Let the ball come to you; do not go and get it.
Hit the ball at belt height — move your feet until it is.
Every ball has to land past the service line.
Finish with the racket pointing at the far fence.
Keep every ball inside the cross-court corridor.
Push the ball toward the wall, do not hit at it.
Brush up the back of the ball toward the top of the fence.
Hit the ball over an imaginary roof a metre above the net.
Step toward the ball as you hit it.
Hit, then step — the ball goes first.
Little hop as they hit, land as it bounces.
Stand as if you are about to be pushed.
Same gap between every hit — count it out loud.
See the ball on the strings before you look up.
Make the ball go slower and land deeper.
Turn so your back pocket faces the wall, then let it come round.
Imagine hitting through two balls in a row toward the target.
Shadow the full swing slowly, then hit at the same speed.
